subject.title: Silent empty tool results in long-running Sonnet 5 sessions after a large tool result

question: Should maintainers treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99524 as the canonical repair path for this issue after rebasing it onto current main, or keep this issue separate until current-main live payload proof confirms the cross-provider failure mode?
rationale: The source gap and user reports strongly point at the same prompt-projection recovery class, but the candidate PR is open and conflicting, and no current-main installed-session proof demonstrates closure yet.

options.title: Adopt or rebase the candidate PR
options.body: Use the candidate PR's non-trailing fresh-result protection as the canonical fix, refresh it for current main, then close this issue only after merged source and live or redacted payload proof.

options.title: Hold for separate live repro
options.body: Keep this issue as its own tracker until a maintainer captures a failing and after-fix provider-bound payload on current main or the rebased fix.

options.title: Split follow-up after the PR lands
options.body: Land the candidate fix for the shared projection gap, then keep only a narrower follow-up if this report still reproduces afterward.

recommendation.title: Adopt or rebase the candidate PR
recommendation.body: Use the candidate PR's non-trailing fresh-result protection as the canonical fix, refresh it for current main, then close this issue only after merged source and live or redacted payload proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current session-scoped prompt projection state and are the best available owner for reconciling the open candidate PR with current main.
